content: 1. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inducers with benzhydrocodone (a prodrug of hydrocodone) may increase plasma concentrations of hydrocodone, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while benzphetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 3. Belladonna alkaloids and benztropine reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Additive anticholinergic adverse effects may occur with concurrent use. Use caution and monitor. 4. Phenobarbital reduces berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 5. Phenobarbital decreases betaxolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. 6. Bethanechol increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 7. Phenobarbital reduces bexagliflozin levels by affecting UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for additional glycemic control if needed. 8. Phenobarbital decreases bexarotene levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Phenobarbital reduces bisoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. 10. Blinatumomab increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The highest risk of drug-drug interactions occurs during the first 9 days of the first cycle and the first 2 days of the second cycle in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates. 11. Phenobarbital decreases bortezomib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Phenobarbital reduces brentuximab vedotin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Phenobarbital and brexanolone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 14. Phenobarbital decreases brexpiprazole levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both drugs increase sedation. 15. Phenobarbital and brimonidine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 16. Phenobarbital reduces brivaracetam levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Both drugs increase sedation. 17. Brodalumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing brodalumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index. 18. Phenobarbital decreases bromocriptine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Phenobarbital and brompheniramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 20. Phenobarbital reduces budesonide levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 21. Phenobarbital and bupivacaine implant may increase each other's toxicity. Local anesthetics may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when used with drugs that also cause this condition. Use caution and monitor. 22. Phenobarbital and buprenorphine both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces buprenorphine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Phenobarbital reduces buprenorphine subdermal implant levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms in patients requiring newly initiated CYP3A4 inducers. Implant removal may be necessary if the inducer cannot be reduced or discontinued. 24. Phenobarbital reduces buprenorphine transdermal levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Phenobarbital reduces buprenorphine long-acting injection levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels and consider transitioning back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments if necessary. 26. Phenobarbital reduces bupropion levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Phenobarbital reduces buspirone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Phenobarbital and butabarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 29. Phenobarbital and butalbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 30. Phenobarbital and butorphanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 31. Phenobarbital reduces cabazitaxel levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 32. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while caffeine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 33. Phenobarbital reduces calcifediol levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Drugs that stimulate microsomal hydroxylation reduce calcifediol's half-life. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Phenobarbital reduces calcitriol levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Phenobarbital reduces canagliflozin levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider using a different antihyperglycemic agent in patients with eGFR <73 mL/min/1.73 m². 36. Phenobarbital reduces cannabidiol levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Cannabidiol increases phenobarbital levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Phenobarbital and captopril may synergistically lower blood pressure. Monitor blood pressure closely. 38. Phenobarbital reduces carbamazepine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Phenobarbital and carbinoxamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 40. Phenobarbital and cariprazine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 41. Phenobarbital and carisoprodol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 42. Phenobarbital reduces carvedilol levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. 43. Phenobarbital reduces celiprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Cenobamate increases phenobarbital levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both drugs increase sedation. 45. Phenobarbital and chloral hydrate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 46. Chloramphenicol increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Phenobarbital and chlordiazepoxide both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces chlordiazepoxide levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Phenobarbital reduces chloroquine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Phenobarbital and chlorpheniramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 50. Phenobarbital and chlorpromazine both increase sedation. Chlorpromazine increases belladonna alkaloid effects via pharmacodynamic synergism. Belladonna alkaloids reduce chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution and monitor. 51. Phenobarbital and chlorzoxazone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 52. Belladonna alkaloids and cisatracurium both reduce cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 53. Phenobarbital reduces cilostazol levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Phenobarbital reduces cinacalcet levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Phenobarbital and cinnarizine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 56. Phenobarbital reduces citalopram levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Phenobarbital and clemastine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 58. Phenobarbital and clobazam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 59. Phenobarbital reduces clomipramine levels by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 60. Phenobarbital and clonazepam both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces clonazepam levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Belladonna alkaloids reduce clozapine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Clozapine increases belladonna alkaloid effects via pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Phenobarbital and codeine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 63. Phenobarbital reduces colchicine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 64. Phenobarbital reduces conivaptan levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Phenobarbital reduces conjugated estrogens levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 66. Phenobarbital reduces cortisone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 67. Phenobarbital reduces crizotinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
